resources.string: Copies your private key to the clipboard, marked as sensitive. Anyone who has it controls your profile, so paste it only where you trust.
Saves your private key to a file you choose, locked with a password you set. You need that password to open the file.
Shares your private key as plain text with an app you choose, after a warning. The encrypted export is safer.
Shows or hides your private key on this screen. It does not copy or share it.
Signs out of this profile on this device. Groups, history and drafts stay, and you can sign back in from the account picker.
Permanently removes this account from this device, including messages, group encryption data and the stored key. You can sign in again with the same key, but past groups are gone.
When on, your published invitation keys are removed from relays as you sign out, so nobody can invite you to new groups while you are signed out.
Opens Share & Connect for this profile. Tap the short key to copy the full public key instead.
Opens the options for this profile picture.

Opens the relays this profile uses. A relay is a server that stores and passes along encrypted messages and public events such as your profile. Here you choose which relays you post to and receive invitations from, and add or remove them. A relay can see public events, but not what your encrypted messages say.

Turns this relay on or off in Where I post, the list of relays that carry your profile and connection info so other people can find you. Your profile is public, so any relay that stores it can read it. At least one relay has to stay in the list.

Turns this relay on or off in Where I receive, the list of relays where people send you invitations to new chats and groups. Invitations are encrypted, so the relay cannot read them. If the list is empty, invitations may not reach you, so at least one relay has to stay on.

Publishes the relay lists marked Missing, Where I post and Where I receive. Other people look these lists up to find your profile and to know where to send you invitations. Until they are published, people may not be able to reach you. Only missing lists are published.
Removes this relay from your relay lists in this setup step. You can undo it right after.
Shows the key packages published for this account, which let others invite you to groups, and lets you manage them.
Lists groups that could not be safely loaded and lets you retry recovery. Nothing is deleted.
Shows agent-stream and MLS signaling events inline in conversations. Meant for debugging.
Reloads the list of quarantined groups. It does not retry recovery.
Retries the shared engine validation for this group. It does not delete history, bypass checks or rejoin the group.
Uses Google Firebase Cloud Messaging to briefly wake White Noise, which then checks securely for messages. Local notifications keep a connection open instead.
Keeps a persistent connection while notifications are on and creates them on this device, instead of using push.
Shares feature use and app performance for all profiles on this device, with a temporary session ID and a resettable installation ID. It never includes account or group IDs.
Shares sanitized technical logs about groups from all profiles on this device with White Noise, separate from usage sharing. Turning it off stops new recording and uploads.
Pulling down on the chat list shows only unread chats. Show all brings the full list back.
Allows automatic downloads on this kind of network. Every matching network rule must allow it, and manual downloads always work.
